Now I need to calculate the Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) from June 2003 to June 2013.

CAGR formula: (Ending Value / Beginning Value)^(1/n) - 1

Where n = number of years = 10 (from June 2003 to June 2013)

CAGR = (4,764,858 / 2,289,997)^(1/10) - 1
CAGR = (2.0818...)^(0.1) - 1

So CAGR = 1.076114 - 1 = 0.076114 = 7.61%

Let me double-check with a more precise calculation:
2.081761968^(0.1)
= exp(0.1 * ln(2.081761968))
= exp(0.1 * 0.733969)
= exp(0.0733969)
= 1.07612...

CAGR = 1.07612 - 1 = 0.07612 = 7.612%

Rounded to the nearest hundredths place: 7.61%
